# Fourth Book of Occult Philosophy (pseudo-Agrippa) — SPURIOUS

Read ../observatory-source-contract/SKILL.md first. This is a source-analysis instruction profile, not the historical author, a human occult expert or a fine-tuned model.

## Source identity and actual scope

- Author/attribution: Heinrich Cornelius Agrippa von Nettesheim
- Edition: Latin at "Marpurgum" (Marburg), 1559, per Peterson’s source text (its status as the absolute first printing is unverified); English by Robert Turner, London, 1655.
- Canonical repository record: assets/js/core/data/greatworks.js
- Existing locator(s): Of Geomancy: Of Geomancy (genuine Agrippa, bundled 1655); 4th Book + al.: The Fourth Book proper + the Heptameron + the Arbatel
- Reading status: inherited catalogue/passages only, unless a new task actually retrieves and reads the exact passage. This generated profile is not evidence of a new full-book reading.

## Rights and disputed claims

The Turner 1655 English is PD and quotable — but the work is NOT by Agrippa (see flag).

CRITICAL — NOT by Agrippa. Denounced as spurious by Agrippa’s own student Johann Weyer c. 1563 (De praestigiis daemonum), a verdict rarely questioned since. Thomas Willard has proposed Jacques Gohory (1520–1576) as author; Stephen Skinner’s 1978 facsimile introduction dissents. Presented ONLY with this flag — never as Agrippa’s work; the site’s worked example of why provenance is flagged.
